text: I now give the floor to his excellency
Abdul Majid Abdul Rahim Muhammad,
Minister of Public Health and Prevention
of Chad.
Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen,
heads of state and government,
Secretary General of the United Nations
Organization, distinguished delegates,
ladies and gentlemen,
the Marshall of Chad Muhammad Idris

Mr. President, your election at the
presidency of the 81st session of the
General Assembly of our shared
organization bears witness to the trust
that the international community has
placed in you and in your leadership.
Please be assured of the full support
the Republic of Chad as you carry out
your term. I would also like to thank
Madame Analina,
outgoing president of the General
Assembly for heading up the work of the
80th regular session so brilliantly at
the a time when he is preparing to move
on from being the head of our
organization. I would like ladies and
gentlemen to pay a very sincere tribute
to the secretary general Mr. Antonio
Gutes. His leadership and constant
commitment to peace, conflict
prevention, and multilateralism
warrant our recognition and respect.
Chad is grateful to him for his ongoing
attention to the challenges that our
country, the lack chad basin and central
Africa are confronted with. Mr.
President, excellencies, ladies and
gentlemen, we are here today at a unique
moment in the history of our
organization.
At a time when the UN is discussing
crucial reforms and multilateralism is
at a crossroads, the topic of this 81st
session, restoring trust,
managing transformation
is a very relevant topic.
It summarizes the expectations of member
states and the peoples of the world in
all of their diversity visav the UN.
Each year we adopt new resolutions and
we reaffirm our commitments. Each year
we renew our faith in multilateralism.
Nonetheless, conflicts persist. People
are still awaiting justice. Will
generations still grow up with fighting
as their backdrop? Mr. President,
excellencies, ladies and gentlemen,
security council reform illustrates
alone this situation and this crisis of
confidence.
For decades now, positions have been
well known. Calls for reform have
stacked up and consultations have
multiplied.
But progress still remains insufficient.
Chad reiterates to this end its complete
support for the common African position
as stipulated in the Ezelwini consensus
and the ST declaration and taken up in
the African model for reform of the
security council presented in April by
Sierra Leon on behalf of the committee
of 10 of the African Union.
Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, Chad
considers that those difficulties facing
multilateralism
stem in part from the cynicism of the
most powerful and from double standards
policies. My country remains committed
to multilateralism that is based on the
UN charter, the sovereign equality of
states, the respect for their
independence, cooperation, and
international solidarity.
Thus, the government of the Republic of
Chad on the 27th of July, 2026
informed the Secretary General of the
United Nations as its depository
of its sovereign and irrevocable
decision to withdraw from the Rome
Statute of the International Criminal
Court.
This decision follows an indepth
consideration of how the court has
functioned since it was set up in 2002.
The data provided by the court and the
lessons learned from that have shown us
that in several states and among their
populations, one can detect that the
focus of the judicial activity of the
court is on developing countries and in
particular on Africa which has become
the target of political
instrumentalization.
I'd like to be perfectly clear here.
This choice does not mean we are
renouncing our responsibilities.
Nor are we becoming a refuge against
justice and even less so are we being
complacent in the face of impunity.
We will continue to strengthen our
national courts and support credible,
independent, and effective African
mechanisms that can protect victims and
prosecute the perpetrators of the most
serious crimes. Excellencies, ladies and
gentlemen, nationally speaking, through
by the grace of God and thanks to the
maturity of its people, Chad remains a
country of peace and stability despite
the numerous domestic challenges it
faces and the crisis that threaten its
borders. The president of the republic
ma the marshall of Chad Muhammad Idris
DebiNo
as guarantor of these institutions
remains determined to maintain peace to
build national cohesion and to create
conditions for sustainable shared
development.
Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen,
today countries in the south are feeling
the full brunt of climate change.
Lake Chad is one of the most salient
symbols of this. It's being vulnerable
directly affects the means of
subsistence of millions of people. We
would therefore urge developed countries
to uphold their commitments in terms of
adaptation, resilience, loss and damages
and technology transfer financing. Mr.
President,
the clear ambition that my country has
for its development can only be achieved
with peace, stability and security in
our region and also in the world.
The security situation in the Sahel and
in the Lake Chad basin demands our
constant attention.
Terrorist groups in the Lake Chad basin,
albeit weakened, continue to plunge our
countries into mourning. Regarding
Libya, Chad is delighted that the
dialogue under the opaces of the special
representative, the secretary general of
the UN has been resumed whilst hoping
for a swift settlement of the dispute.
in the Central African Republic. Chad
has discreetly and consistently striven
for mediation. This led on the 19th of
April 20125 to the signature of a
ceasefire agreement between the Central
African Republic government and two of
the main armed groups of the country.
More recently in Haiti, Chad responded
to the call from our organization.
We decided to deploy
1,500 service personnel to the gang
suppression force authorized by the
security council and that is about a
quarter of the planned amount
through its constant vision. For years
now, Chad has remained one of the main
African contributors of troops to
peacekeeping operations throughout the
world. Your excellencies, ladies and
gentlemen, this solidarity that we
project outwards is something we also
experience every day within our own
borders.
Since April 2023, more than a million
Sudin refugees have crossed our eastern
border, fleeing a bloody conflict
along with displaced persons from other
regional crises. My country is currently
hosting more than 2 million people
who've been forcibly displaced.
One person out of 17 in my country is
today a refugee.
From this rostrm, I would like to
solemnly reiterate and reaffirm Chad's
position regarding the Sudin conflict.
Our country has observed since the very
first day of the war strict, absolute
and unchanged neutrality.
I would like to say this very firmly.
My country does not support any of the
parties to the conflict in Sudan and in
no way authorizes the use of its
territory or its infrastructure to their
benefit.
Chad reiterates its commitment to peace
in Sudan and reiterates its support for
all initiatives, including those of the
Quad and the Quintet,
seeking to establish a ceasefire and to
promote dialogue between the waring
parties.
Your excellencies, ladies and gentlemen,
I cannot
now remain silent regarding the serious
nature of that which is directly
affecting our sovereignty. Over recent
days, the energy east province within
our country has been the theater of air
strikes linked to the conflict in Sudan.
Chad condemns in the strongest possible
terms these new incursions. They are an
unacceptable violation of our
territorial integrity and Chad reserves
the right to take all necessary measures
in line with international law to
protect its population and its
sovereignty if this occurs again.
Mr. President, your excellencies, ladies
and gentlemen,
I would also from this rostroom like to
stress how concerned my country is with
the crisis in the Gulf region and the
repercussions of this on the global
economy. Loyal to the principles of the
charter, Chad rejects any act of
aggression against a sovereign state
and condemns to this end the air strikes
against the Islamic Republic of Iran.
And along the same lines, Chan very
firmly condemns the Iranian attacks
against the fraternal fraternal
countries of the Gulf Cooperation
Council and Jordan as well as the drone
attack on the 29th of July in the
Egyptian port of Damet.
We would urge all parties to demonstrate
restraint and to promote dialogue
regarding the Middle East. Chad remains
seriously concerned by ongoing violence
and humanitarian suffering in Gaza.
Sticking to its unwavering position, my
country reiterates its unfailing
commitment to the right of the
Palestinian people to have their own
state in the 1967 borders alongside a
state of Israel
that lives in peace and security.
As we do each year on this same
occasion, we call once again for the
lifting of the economic and trade
embargo imposed on Cuba and on its
people.
Mr. President, your excellencies, ladies
and gentlemen, the theme
restoring trust,
managing transformation
first and foremost requires consistency
between what we declare here and what we
do when the microphones are turned off.
The choices that Chad makes, the
responsibilities that it shoulders, and
the sacrifices that it makes,
all stem from the belief that
multilateralism
only has a future if it knows how to
reform if it can correct any imbalances
and if it can be applied if rather the
same principles can be applied to all.
Chad remains firmly committed to the
ideals that prevailed at the time of the
establishment of the United Nations.
Despite disappointments, we still
believe in the force of law against the
right to use force. We believe in a more
representative organization of the world
as it is now, more effective in its work
and truly delivering for all.
Long live international cooperation.
Long live Chad. I thank you.
I thank the Minister of Public Health
